public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 484

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/484](https://www.erdosproblems.com/484)
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [ESS89] Erdős, P., Sárközy, A., and Sós, V. T., *On a conjecture of Roth and some related
  problems. I*. (1989), 47-59.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos484

open scoped Classical in
/--
Prove that there exists an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, whenever $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is
$k$-coloured (and $N$ is large enough depending on $k$) then there are at least $cN$ many
integers in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ which are representable as a monochromatic sum (that is, $a+b$
where $a,b\in \{1,\ldots,N\}$ are in the same colour class and $a\neq b$).

A conjecture of Roth. Solved by Erdős, Sárközy, and Sós [ESS89], who in fact prove that
there are at least $\frac{N}{2}-O(N^{1-1/2^{k+1}})$ many even numbers which are of this form.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos484.lean"]
theorem erdos_484 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N → ∀ f : ℕ → Fin k,
      c * N ≤ (((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter fun n =>
        ∃ a ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ∃ b ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
          a ≠ b ∧ f a = f b ∧ a + b = n).card : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos484

reformulations.difference: The Lean theorem quantifies over total colourings ℕ → Fin k, whereas the original finite formulation colours only {1,…,N}.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every interval colouring extends to ℕ by assigning colour 0 outside the interval; 0 < k ensures that this colour exists. Conversely, every total colouring restricts to an interval colouring. The representation predicate uses colours only at summands inside the interval, so restriction and extension preserve exactly the finite set being counted. The full equivalence was proved as Review484.statement_models_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1961-22.pdf — Erdős, Some unsolved problems (1961), §I, problem 16, p. 230.
https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf — Erdős, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory (1980), p. 112.
https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1989-14.pdf — Erdős–Sárközy–Sós, On a conjecture of Roth and some related problems I (1989), definitions (1)–(3), Theorem 1, and subsequent remarks.
review.notes: Reviewed the file's sole declaration, including quantifier dependencies, positivity, interval endpoints, distinct summands, cardinality, coercions, and boundary cases. It faithfully states Roth's conjecture, and the solved category agrees with ESS89. The printed sources' strict inequalities are equivalent to the weak inequalities here after reducing the existential positive constant and adjusting the threshold. Computations for one-colour and parity colourings at N=0,…,10 agreed with the intended sets; the computational expression was proved equal to the theorem's expression. The exact linked proof compiled with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Its floored bound implies the repository's real-valued bound by replacing c with c/2 and increasing N₀; this bridge also compiled with only those axioms. The erdosproblems.com page returned a Cloudflare challenge despite a descriptive User-Agent, so verification relied on all three cited primary papers instead. The file under review was not modified.
